statement: After an integrity check, hand the next tool the file you hashed under a name you chose, never a name an untrusted source supplied, because the tool may re-parse the name as something other than a path. 2026-11-09, cejel #696 (issue 686), my own error, found by review Pass B: each Action step ran tarball=$(npm pack ...), hashed $tarball, then ran npm install ./$tarball. npm builds that name from the registry manifest, so a registry serving the genuine bytes under version 1@evil.example:r produced x-1@evil.example:r.tgz. The sha512 matched the pin and npm install then read the argument as a git spec (git ls-remote, unknown git error, exit 128). I had written that the step installs from the checked file. Fix (#696): mv -- "$tarball" pnpm.tgz, hash pnpm.tgz, install ./pnpm.tgz; reproduced with an npm shim, old step exit 128, new step installs the checked file.
